title: Stretch an elastic wire
hook: Change tension force and predict tensile strain.
misconception: tensile strain stays fixed when tension force doubles.
objective: Apply strain = F/(AY) to compare tensile strain when tension force changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a uniform wire in its linear elastic regime with fixed area and Young modulus, strain = F/(AY). When tension force doubles, tensile strain becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model strain = F/(AY); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a uniform wire in its linear elastic regime with fixed area and Young modulus, with a nonzero initial result. If tension force triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on tensile strain?
recall.why: Apply strain = F/(AY) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
